Why rewards cards carry higher APRs than plain cards
The bank's business model: rewards funded by people who carry balances
If you carry a balance: the payoff-first plan before any rewards talk
Autopay-in-full as the default setting, not an option

topics.title: Buying a House Soon? Stop Applying for Cards
topics.thesis: Underwriters read recent credit-seeking as risk, and no sign-up bonus is worth a worse mortgage rate. When to freeze applications, for how long, and what's safe to keep doing.
key_points: Why mortgage underwriting punishes recent inquiries and new accounts
The freeze window: months before application through closing
The rate math: a fraction of a percent on a mortgage dwarfs any bonus
What's fine during the freeze: using existing cards, paying in full
Restarting responsibly after the keys are in hand

topics.title: Authorized Users: Family Perk or $175 Line Item?
topics.thesis: Adding a partner to your card ranges from free and valuable to a paid add-on that quietly raises your effective fee. The household math on authorized users, card by card type.
key_points: What an authorized user gets: purchasing, sometimes perks, sometimes lounges
Where AU fees now stand on premium cards, and what they buy
Credit-building for the AU: how the account reports to their file
When two separate cards beat one card plus paid AUs
The risk column: shared spending, one person's liability
